source.title: Directions of Curvature as an Explanation for Loss of Plasticity
source.authors: Alex Lewandowski; Haruto Tanaka; Dale Schuurmans; Marlos C. Machado

record.tranche_reason: The study tests training-error behavior under continual task changes, including random-label CIFAR-10 and network scaling, extending the claim to continual learning. It does not test the stated fixed-dataset recipes directly.
record.gate_note: The paper reports task-end error and how it changes across tasks. Its central measure is loss of plasticity, not whether a model reaches zero training error on a fixed dataset.
record.test_reason: The study measures worsening task-end error after repeated distribution changes, rather than convergence to near-zero classification error from random initialization on a fixed CIFAR dataset. Its scaling, curvature and regularization results do not test the specific comparisons in V2–V6.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors argue that loss of curvature directions consistently explains loss of plasticity across their tested settings, based on co-occurrence measured primarily through an empirical Fisher approximation to Hessian rank. Scaling delays but does not eliminate plasticity loss, while effective regularization preserves plasticity and curvature. Their Wasserstein regularizer achieves lower error on harder benchmarks with less sensitivity to regularization strength.
record.recipe_differences: Continual supervised learning with periodic task changes and task-end error measurement; the claim concerns training to low classification error on fixed benchmark datasets.
record.method_sensitivity: Network width and depth delay loss of plasticity; regularization changes the ResNet18 outcome.

fits_no_version.finding: Increasing width or depth delays loss of plasticity and marginally lowers the eventual error plateau, without eliminating it.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Scaling networks can delay deterioration in task-end learning performance across continual task sequences.

fits_no_version.finding: ResNet18 with batch normalization loses plasticity on successive random-label CIFAR-10 tasks without regularization; regularization preserves performance at an error slightly above the unregularized model's best.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large residual networks can lose plasticity under repeated label changes, and regularization can mitigate that deterioration.

fits_no_version.finding: Loss of plasticity co-occurs with declining effective Hessian rank, estimated using an empirical Fisher approximation; effective regularizers also preserve these curvature directions.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Declining curvature directions accompany loss of plasticity across the tested continual-learning settings.

record.problems: The relevant scaling and ResNet results are presented in figures without numeric task-end error values in the text. The scaling figure's dataset is not stated in the supplied text. The experiments concern continual task changes and do not establish absolute error on a fixed dataset.

untested.parts: Convergence to zero or near-zero training classification error from random initialization on fixed CIFAR-10 or CIFAR-100 datasets, including label corruption and the stated model-size and training-recipe qualifications.
Spurious local minima and the effect of one or two extra student neurons in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.
Depth degradation in plain batch-normalized convolutional networks; matched identity-shortcut comparisons; very deep tanh initialization and Fixup exceptions.
Comparisons of initialization schemes, signal or gradient propagation, training speed and trainable depth. Regularizing toward an initialization distribution does not test these comparisons.
Learning rates relative to the initial stability threshold, catapult recovery, divergence and full-batch edge-of-stability dynamics. Hessian-rank measurements do not establish these effects.
Matched training-speed and learning-rate-tolerance comparisons with and without batch normalization, including Fixup.

record.verdict_notes: No verdicts apply to V1–V6. Continual deterioration under a fixed update budget does not contradict successful optimization from random initialization on a stationary dataset.

versions.untested_parts: Fixed-dataset training from random initialization; zero or near-zero absolute training error; CIFAR-100; comparison of SGD and Adam; early stopping.

rows.subject: neural network
rows.operation_detail: Varied network depth while holding width at 800.
rows.measure: Task-end error across tasks; loss of plasticity
rows.value: Increasing depth delays loss of plasticity and marginally lowers the error plateau, but does not eliminate loss of plasticity.
rows.note: The text summarizes the depth sweep; it does not give absolute error values or identify the dataset for this figure.
rows.check: The reported depth effect concerns preservation of plasticity across tasks. It establishes neither V1's near-zero training error nor V3's depth degradation comparison between plain batch-normalized and residual networks. Figure 7's dataset and absolute errors are unspecified in the supplied text.

rows.subject: neural network
rows.operation_detail: Varied hidden-layer width while holding depth at 4.
rows.measure: Task-end error across tasks; loss of plasticity
rows.value: Increasing width delays loss of plasticity and marginally lowers the error plateau, but does not eliminate loss of plasticity.
rows.note: The text summarizes the width sweep; it does not give absolute error values or identify the dataset for this figure.
rows.check: Width delays worsening task-end error, but this does not measure V1's near-zero training error or V2's spurious local minima in two-layer ReLU teacher-student problems.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on successive random-label CIFAR-10 tasks without regularization.
rows.measure: Task-end error across tasks; loss of plasticity
rows.value: Loss of plasticity still occurs without regularization; the ResNet is not able to maintain its initial error.
rows.note: This is a continual task sequence; the text does not report whether absolute training error is near zero.
rows.check: ResNet18 is warm-started across successive random-label tasks with a fixed 20-epoch budget. Increasing task-end error does not establish failure to reach near-zero error from random initialization. Batch normalization is present, but there is no matched comparison without it.

rows.subject: ResNet18
rows.operation_detail: Trained on successive random-label CIFAR-10 tasks with regularization.
rows.baseline: ResNet18 without regularization; exact error not stated
rows.value: With regularization, the ResNet achieves an error level slightly higher than the best error that the unregularized version can achieve.
rows.note: The comparison does not establish absolute training error or whether it is near zero.
rows.check: The relative error comparison under regularization gives no absolute training classification error. The 0.005 regularization strength is correct; the record's numbers_found value of 1/1 is unsupported.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
